question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> be a set with exactly <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> elements and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> be a set with exactly <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn></math> elements. If <math><mi>α</mi></math> is the number of one-one functions from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>Y</mi></math> and <math><mi>β</mi></math> is the number of onto functions from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>X</mi></math>, then the value of <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is _____-.

solution.text:
nX=5
nY=7
α→ Number of one-one function =7C5×5!
β→ Number of onto function Y to X

So, β=7!3!4!×5!+7!2!33!×5!=7C3+3. 7C35!=4×7C3×5!
β-α5!=4×7C3-7C5=4×35-21=119
